draft.title: How speakers position listeners
card: Speakers position listeners: they use spoken techniques to lead the audience to feel or respond in a certain way.
Tone
the speaker's voice and attitude, such as calm, angry or warm. A serious tone can make a listener take the issue seriously.
Emotive words and anecdotes
emotive words stir feelings, as in "a shameful waste". An anecdote is a short personal story that makes an issue feel real and close.
Direct address
speaking to the audience as "you" or "we", as in "You can make a difference". It makes listeners feel included and responsible.
draft.remember: Speakers use tone, emotive words, anecdotes and direct address to lead listeners to respond a certain way.

a.q: A student speaker tells her audience, "Each of you walks past this litter daily, and you can fix it." Which technique is mainly used?
opts: Direct address, to make listeners feel responsible
An anecdote, to tell a personal story
Emotive words, to stir anger in the listeners
Tone, to sound calm and relaxed to the listeners
a.why: The speaker talks straight to the audience using "you", which makes each listener feel responsible. There is no story, so it is not an anecdote.
a.clue: Look at the words that speak straight to the audience.

b.q: Leo tells his class how his gran was left waiting an hour for a bus in the rain. He then asks them to support better bus services. What is the main effect of his story?
opts: It makes the problem feel real and builds sympathy
It speaks to each listener as "you" to give them a duty
It shows a calm tone so listeners trust his facts
It uses a strong emotive word to make listeners angry
b.why: A short personal story is an anecdote. It makes the issue feel real and builds sympathy for people affected. Direct address would need words like "you" spoken to the audience, which the story does not use.
b.clue: Ask what kind of technique a short personal story is.
